# 1. Scope of analysis

This notebook implements a fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) to examine which configurations of Urban Quality of Life (UQoL) dimensions are associated with high and low levels of perceived residential satisfaction across Barcelona's neighbourhoods. The analysis uses the composite dimension scores produced by PCA in the preceding chapter.

A key design decision in this analysis is the inclusion of all 73 neighbourhoods rather than restricting it to the 11 classified as tourist areas. This choice responds to two complementary concerns. First, a methodological one: with 7 UQoL conditions and only 11 cases, the case-to-condition ratio would be critically low, producing extremely limited diversity and potentially false results (Marx & Dușa, 2011). Second, and more importantly, a conceptual one: tourism does not operate in isolation. Including all neighbourhoods to then treat the tourism classification as an additional context layer in the analysis,allows the method to identify whether tourism combines with specific UQoL profiles to produce satisfaction or dissatisfaction, rather than merely asking what UQoL patterns exist among tourist areas. In other words, the question shifts from "among tourist neighbourhoods, which UQoL configurations matter?" to "does the presence or absence of tourism development, in combination with particular UQoL configurations, form part of the pathways to high or low residential satisfaction?"

This framing is consistent with the dissertation's theoretical model, which positions tourism as a contextual factor — a conditioning element that modulates the relationship between objective living conditions and subjective satisfaction, rather than a direct cause of quality of life in itself. Crucially, non-tourist neighbourhoods serve as a comparison population that strengthens the analytical power of the design: they allow QCA to distinguish configurations that are specific to tourist areas from those that are general patterns across the city.

# 2. Data import

The input data are the aggregated composite indicators produced by PCA, containing one row per neighbourhood and one composite score per UQoL dimension, together with the neighbourhood satisfaction score and tourism classification. The file is read from the PCA output directory relative to the project root.

```{r load-data}
csv_path <- here("1_PCA", "Results", "Aggregated",
                 "aggregated_indicators_by_neighbourhood.csv")

# Verify the file exists before attempting to read it
if (!file.exists(csv_path)) {
  cat("here() resolves to:", here(), "\n")
  cat("Expected file at:", csv_path, "\n")
  stop(paste(
    "File not found. Please ensure the PCA notebook has been run first",
    "so that the aggregated CSV exists in 1_PCA/Results/Aggregated/.",
    "If the file is elsewhere, set csv_path manually before this chunk."
  ))
}

qca_raw <- read.csv(csv_path, header = TRUE, sep = ";")
```

Because the source CSV was produced by `write.csv2()` (which uses semicolons as field separators and commas as decimal marks), all numeric columns require conversion to ensure correct parsing.

```{r clean-decimals}
# Identify columns that need decimal conversion
numeric_cols <- c("satisfaction", "Economic", "Healthcare", "Housing",
                  "Infrastructure", "Mobility", "Social", "Urban")

for (col in numeric_cols) {
  qca_raw[[col]] <- as.numeric(gsub(",", ".", qca_raw[[col]]))
}
```

A preview of the loaded data confirms the structure.

```{r data-preview, echo=FALSE}
head(qca_raw)
cat(paste("\nTotal neighbourhoods:", nrow(qca_raw)))
cat(paste("\nTourist neighbourhoods:",
          sum(qca_raw$Barrio.turístico.en.2023 == "Yes")))
cat(paste("\nNon-tourist neighbourhoods:",
          sum(qca_raw$Barrio.turístico.en.2023 == "No")))
```

# 3. Data preparation

The working dataset retains the neighbourhood identifier, the tourism classification, the satisfaction outcome, and the seven UQoL dimension scores. Tourism status is converted to a binary numeric variable (1 = tourist neighbourhood, 0 = non-tourist).

```{r prepare-data}
qca_data <- qca_raw %>%
  select(codi_barri, nom_barri,
         Barrio.turístico.en.2023,
         satisfaction,
         Economic, Healthcare, Housing,
         Infrastructure, Mobility, Social, Urban) %>%
  mutate(Tourism = ifelse(Barrio.turístico.en.2023 == "Yes", 1, 0))

```

# 4. Calibration

Calibration transforms the raw scores into fuzzy-set membership values ranging from 0 (full non-membership) to 1 (full membership), with 0.5 as the crossover point of maximum ambiguity.

## 4.1 Calibration approach

Three considerations guide the calibration strategy.

First, the UQoL composite scores are PCA-derived standardised values with a mean of approximately zero and no inherent substantive anchors; therefore, a percentile-based approach is used for the conditions. The calibration uses the full 73-neighbourhood distribution, which establishes a city-wide baseline. This is methodologically important: if calibration were performed only on the 11 tourist neighbourhoods, a neighbourhood with the highest Housing score among tourist areas might still represent a mediocre position city-wide. By anchoring to the full distribution, membership values reflect whether a neighbourhood genuinely performs well or poorly relative to Barcelona as a whole, not merely relative to other tourist areas.

Second, satisfaction is measured on a 0–10 scale with a known interpretation. The crossover point is set at the city-wide median, while the full membership and full non-membership thresholds are set at the 75th and 25th percentiles, respectively. This provides a meaningful distinction between neighbourhoods where residents are more satisfied than average and those where they are less so.

## 4.2 Calibrate the outcome

```{r calibrate-outcome}
# Satisfaction thresholds based on the full distribution
sat_q25 <- quantile(qca_data$satisfaction, 0.25)
sat_q50 <- quantile(qca_data$satisfaction, 0.50)
sat_q75 <- quantile(qca_data$satisfaction, 0.75)

cat(paste("Satisfaction calibration thresholds:\n"))
cat(paste("  Full non-membership (Q25):", sat_q25, "\n"))
cat(paste("  Crossover point    (Q50):", sat_q50, "\n"))
cat(paste("  Full membership    (Q75):", sat_q75, "\n"))

qca_data$SATISF <- calibrate(qca_data$satisfaction,
                              type = "fuzzy",
                              thresholds = c(sat_q25, sat_q50, sat_q75))

```

## 4.3 Calibrate the UQoL conditions

```{r calibrate-conditions}
# Define condition labels (uppercase for QCA convention)
cond_labels <- c("ECON", "HLTH", "HOUS", "INFR", "MOBI", "SOCI", "URBN")
names(cond_labels) <- conditions

# Store thresholds for reporting
calibration_log <- data.frame(
  Condition = character(),
  Q25 = numeric(),
  Q50 = numeric(),
  Q75 = numeric(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (v in conditions) {
  fz_name <- cond_labels[v]
  q25 <- quantile(qca_data[[v]], 0.25)
  q50 <- quantile(qca_data[[v]], 0.50)
  q75 <- quantile(qca_data[[v]], 0.75)

  calibration_log <- rbind(calibration_log,
                           data.frame(Condition = v, Q25 = q25, Q50 = q50, Q75 = q75))

  qca_data[[fz_name]] <- calibrate(qca_data[[v]],
                                    type = "fuzzy",
                                    thresholds = c(q25, q50, q75))
}

```

## 4.4 Calibration summary

The table below summarises the calibration thresholds applied to each condition and the outcome.

```{r calibration-summary}
# Add satisfaction row
calibration_log <- rbind(
  calibration_log,
  data.frame(Condition = "Satisfaction", Q25 = sat_q25, Q50 = sat_q50, Q75 = sat_q75)
)

print(calibration_log, row.names = FALSE)

# Save calibration log
write.csv(calibration_log,
          here("2_QCA", "Results", "Calibration", "calibration_thresholds.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

## 4.5 Post-calibration diagnostics

A check is performed to ensure that no case falls exactly on the 0.5 crossover point, which would create ambiguity in the truth table assignment. If any case does, a small constant is conventionally added (Ragin, 2008).

```{r check-crossover}
fz_cols <- c("SATISF", cond_labels)

for (col in fz_cols) {
  n_at_05 <- sum(qca_data[[col]] == 0.5, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n_at_05 > 0) {
    cat(paste("WARNING:", n_at_05, "case(s) at 0.5 in", col,
              "— adding 0.001 to resolve ambiguity.\n"))
    qca_data[[col]][qca_data[[col]] == 0.5] <- 0.501
  }
}

# Negated outcome computed AFTER the 0.5 correction,
# so that SATISF + SATISF_NEG = 1 for every case
qca_data$SATISF_NEG <- 1 - qca_data$SATISF
```

```{r preview-calibrated, echo=FALSE}
tourist_preview <- qca_data %>%
  filter(Tourism == 1) %>%
  select(nom_barri, satisfaction, SATISF, ECON, HLTH, HOUS, INFR, MOBI, SOCI, URBN)

print(tourist_preview, row.names = FALSE)
```

# 5. Analysis of necessary conditions

Before examining sufficiency (which combinations of conditions lead to the outcome), it is standard practice in QCA to test whether any single condition is individually necessary for the outcome. A condition is considered necessary when its consistency score is at or above 0.9 (Ragin, 2008; Schneider & Wagemann, 2012).

## 5.1 Necessary conditions for high satisfaction

```{r necessity-high}
# Define the condition columns for analysis
cond_cols <- c("ECON", "HLTH", "HOUS", "INFR", "MOBI", "SOCI", "URBN")

# Test necessity of each condition and its negation for HIGH satisfaction
nec_high <- pof(
  setms  = qca_data[, cond_cols],
  outcome = qca_data$SATISF,
  relation = "necessity"
)

cat("=== Necessary conditions for HIGH satisfaction ===\n")
print(nec_high)
```

```{r necessity-high-negated}
# Also test negated conditions (absence of a condition)
negated_conds <- 1 - qca_data[, cond_cols]
names(negated_conds) <- paste0("not_", cond_cols)

nec_high_neg <- pof(
  setms  = negated_conds,
  outcome = qca_data$SATISF,
  relation = "necessity"
)

cat("=== Necessary conditions for HIGH satisfaction (negated conditions) ===\n")
print(nec_high_neg)
```

## 5.2 Necessary conditions for low satisfaction

```{r necessity-low}
nec_low <- pof(
  setms  = qca_data[, cond_cols],
  outcome = qca_data$SATISF_NEG,
  relation = "necessity"
)

cat("=== Necessary conditions for LOW satisfaction ===\n")
print(nec_low)
```

```{r necessity-low-negated}
nec_low_neg <- pof(
  setms  = negated_conds,
  outcome = qca_data$SATISF_NEG,
  relation = "necessity"
)

cat("=== Necessary conditions for LOW satisfaction (negated conditions) ===\n")
print(nec_low_neg)
```

```{r save-necessity}
# Save necessity results
sink(here("2_QCA", "Results", "Necessity", "necessity_analysis.txt"))
cat("=== NECESSARY CONDITIONS FOR HIGH SATISFACTION ===\n\n")
cat("Presence of conditions:\n")
print(nec_high)
cat("\nAbsence of conditions:\n")
print(nec_high_neg)
cat("\n\n=== NECESSARY CONDITIONS FOR LOW SATISFACTION ===\n\n")
cat("Presence of conditions:\n")
print(nec_low)
cat("\nAbsence of conditions:\n")
print(nec_low_neg)
sink()
```

# 6. Sufficiency analysis — high satisfaction

The sufficiency analysis identifies configurations of conditions that are consistently associated with the outcome. This involves constructing a truth table, setting consistency and frequency thresholds, and performing logical minimisation.

```{r}
# QCA specification shared by Sections 6, 7 and 10
incl_cut_main <- 0.80
pri_cut_main  <- 0.50   #  minimum PRI floor to flag simultaneous subset relations
dir_exp_high  <- "ECON, HLTH, HOUS, INFR, MOBI, SOCI, URBN"
dir_exp_low   <- "~ECON, ~HLTH, ~HOUS, ~INFR, ~MOBI, ~SOCI, ~URBN"
```


## 6.1 Truth table for high satisfaction

The truth table groups cases by their configuration of condition memberships and reports the consistency and frequency of each observed configuration.

```{r truth-table-high}
tt_high <- truthTable(
  data      = qca_data,
  outcome   = "SATISF",
  conditions = cond_cols,
  incl.cut  = incl_cut_main,# Consistency threshold for sufficiency
  pri.cut   = pri_cut_main,
  n.cut     = 1,          # Minimum frequency: 1 case per configuration
  complete  = TRUE,       # Include logical remainders
  show.cases = TRUE,
  sort.by   = c("incl", "n")
)

tt_high
```

The proportion of observed vs. logically possible configurations is reported below. With 7 conditions, 2^7 = 128 configurations are possible.

```{r diversity-high}
n_possible <- 2^length(cond_cols)
n_observed <- sum(tt_high$tt$n > 0)

cat(paste("Logically possible configurations:", n_possible, "\n"))
cat(paste("Observed configurations:", n_observed, "\n"))
cat(paste("Logical remainders:", n_possible - n_observed, "\n"))
cat(paste("Proportion observed:",
          round(n_observed / n_possible * 100, 1), "%\n"))
```

## 6.2 Logical minimisation — high satisfaction

Three solution types are produced: the complex (conservative) solution, which makes no assumptions about unobserved configurations; the parsimonious solution, which uses all logical remainders; and the intermediate solution, which incorporates directional expectations derived from theory.

The directional expectations are as follows: higher values in all seven UQoL dimensions are expected to contribute to high satisfaction, based on the theoretical framework developed in Chapter II, in which each dimension is defined as a positive contributor to urban quality of life.

**Note on interpretation:** setting a directional expectation does *not* force the condition to appear in the solution. It only determines which logical remainders (unobserved configurations) may be used as simplifying assumptions during minimisation. The actual solution paths are derived from the observed data.

```{r minimise-high-complex}
# Complex (conservative) solution — no simplifying assumptions
sol_high_complex <- minimize(
  tt_high,
  details    = TRUE,
  show.cases = TRUE
)

cat("=== COMPLEX SOLUTION — HIGH SATISFACTION ===\n")
print(sol_high_complex)
```

```{r minimise-high-parsimonious}
# Parsimonious solution — uses all logical remainders
sol_high_pars <- minimize(
  tt_high,
  include    = "?",
  details    = TRUE,
  show.cases = TRUE
)

cat("=== PARSIMONIOUS SOLUTION — HIGH SATISFACTION ===\n")
print(sol_high_pars)
```

```{r minimise-high-intermediate}
# Intermediate solution — incorporates directional expectations
# All conditions expected positive (presence contributes to outcome)
# eQMC + row dominance + first minimal solution only
cat("=== Intermediate solution ===\n")
## === Intermediate solution ===
sol_high_inter <- tryCatch(
  minimize(tt_high, include = "?", details = TRUE, show.cases = TRUE,
           dir.exp = dir_exp_high,
           method = "eQMC", row.dom = FALSE, first.min = FALSE),
  
  error = function(e) {
    cat(paste("FAILED:", e$message, "\n"))
    NULL
  }
)

if (!is.null(sol_high_inter)) {
  cat("=== INTERMEDIATE SOLUTION - HIGH SATISFACTION ===\n")
  print(sol_high_inter)
}

```

## 6.3 Save high satisfaction results

```{r save-high}
# Save truth table as CSV
tt_high_df <- as.data.frame(tt_high$tt)
write.csv(tt_high_df,
          here("2_QCA", "Results", "Sufficiency", "truth_table_high_satisfaction.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# Save solutions to text
sink(here("2_QCA", "Results", "Sufficiency", "solutions_high_satisfaction.txt"))
cat("=== COMPLEX SOLUTION ===\n\n")
print(sol_high_complex)
cat("\n\n=== PARSIMONIOUS SOLUTION ===\n\n")
print(sol_high_pars)
cat("\n\n=== INTERMEDIATE SOLUTION ===\n\n")
print(sol_high_inter)
sink()
```

# 7. Sufficiency analysis — low satisfaction

The same procedure is applied to the negated outcome (low satisfaction), allowing identification of configurations associated with dissatisfaction.

## 7.1 Truth table for low satisfaction

```{r truth-table-low}
tt_low <- truthTable(
  data      = qca_data,
  outcome   = "SATISF_NEG",
  conditions = cond_cols,
  incl.cut  = incl_cut_main,
  pri.cut   = pri_cut_main,
  n.cut     = 1,
  complete  = TRUE,
  show.cases = TRUE,
  sort.by   = c("incl", "n")
)

tt_low
```

## 7.2 Logical minimisation — low satisfaction

For the negated outcome, directional expectations are reversed: the absence of high UQoL conditions (i.e., low dimensional values) is expected to contribute to low satisfaction. 

```{r minimise-low-complex}
sol_low_complex <- minimize(
  tt_low,
  details    = TRUE,
  show.cases = TRUE
)

cat("=== COMPLEX SOLUTION — LOW SATISFACTION ===\n")
print(sol_low_complex)
```

```{r minimise-low-parsimonious}
sol_low_pars <- minimize(
  tt_low,
  include    = "?",
  details    = TRUE,
  show.cases = TRUE
)

cat("=== PARSIMONIOUS SOLUTION — LOW SATISFACTION ===\n")
print(sol_low_pars)
```

```{r minimise-low-intermediate}
# For negated outcome: absence of conditions expected to contribute to LOW satisfaction
# eQMC + row dominance + first minimal solution only
cat("=== Intermediate solution ===\n")
## === Intermediate solution ===
sol_low_inter <- tryCatch(
  minimize(tt_low, include = "?", details = TRUE, show.cases = TRUE,
           dir.exp = dir_exp_low,
           method = "eQMC", row.dom = FALSE, first.min = FALSE),
  error = function(e) {
    cat(paste("FAILED:", e$message, "\n"))
    NULL
  }
)

if (!is.null(sol_low_inter)) {
  cat("=== INTERMEDIATE SOLUTION - LOW SATISFACTION ===\n")
  print(sol_low_inter)
}

```

## 7.3 Save low satisfaction results

```{r save-low}
tt_low_df <- as.data.frame(tt_low$tt)
write.csv(tt_low_df,
          here("2_QCA", "Results", "Sufficiency", "truth_table_low_satisfaction.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

sink(here("2_QCA", "Results", "Sufficiency", "solutions_low_satisfaction.txt"))
cat("=== COMPLEX SOLUTION ===\n\n")
print(sol_low_complex)
cat("\n\n=== PARSIMONIOUS SOLUTION ===\n\n")
print(sol_low_pars)
cat("\n\n=== INTERMEDIATE SOLUTION ===\n\n")
print(sol_low_inter)
sink()
```

# 8. Tourism context mapping
Tourism dimension is added as an analytical variable based on identifier. The objective is to determine whether tourist neighbourhoods cluster in specific configurations to high or low satisfaction, or whether they are distributed across the same configurations as non-tourist areas.

## 8.1 Build case lookup table

```{r prepare-tourism-lookup}

case_lookup <- qca_data %>%
  mutate(case_id = as.integer(rownames(qca_data))) %>%
  select(case_id, codi_barri, nom_barri, Tourism, satisfaction)

# Safeguard: every case ID must be a valid integer and unique
stopifnot(!anyNA(case_lookup$case_id),
          !anyDuplicated(case_lookup$case_id))

cat("=== Tourist neighbourhoods and their QCA case IDs ===\n")

print(case_lookup %>% filter(Tourism == 1), row.names = FALSE)
```

## 8.2 Map truth table configurations to tourism status
For each configuration that passed the consistency threshold (OUT = 1), the code identifies the cases it contains and flags tourist neighbourhoods.

```{r}
cat("=====================================================\n")
cat("  HIGH SATISFACTION - Cases in sufficient configs\n")
cat("=====================================================\n\n")

tt_high_pass <- tt_high$tt[tt_high$tt$OUT == 1, ]

for (i in seq_len(nrow(tt_high_pass))) {
  row <- tt_high_pass[i, ]
  case_str <- as.character(row$cases)
  case_ids <- as.integer(unlist(strsplit(gsub(" ", "", case_str), ",")))
  cases_info <- case_lookup %>% filter(case_id %in% case_ids)
  
  # Extract condition values safely
  config_vals <- as.numeric(row[cond_cols])
  config_parts <- ifelse(config_vals == 1, cond_cols, paste0("~", cond_cols))
  config_label <- paste(config_parts, collapse = "*")
  
  n_tourist <- sum(cases_info$Tourism == 1)
  n_total   <- nrow(cases_info)
  
  # Extract and convert consistency to numeric
  consistency <- as.numeric(row$incl)
  
  cat(paste0("Config: ", config_label, "\n"))
  cat(paste0("  Consist: ", round(consistency, 3),
             "  |  N=", n_total,
             "  |  Tourist: ", n_tourist, "/", n_total,
             " (", round(n_tourist / n_total * 100, 0), "%)\n"))
  
  for (j in seq_len(nrow(cases_info))) {
    marker <- ifelse(cases_info$Tourism[j] == 1, " [T]", "")
    cat(paste0("    #", cases_info$case_id[j], " ",
               cases_info$nom_barri[j],
               " (sat=", round(cases_info$satisfaction[j], 2), ")",
               marker, "\n"))
  }
  cat("\n")
}
```



```{r}
cat("=====================================================\n")
cat("  LOW SATISFACTION - Cases in sufficient configs\n")
cat("=====================================================\n\n")
tt_low_pass <- tt_low$tt[tt_low$tt$OUT == 1, ]

for (i in seq_len(nrow(tt_low_pass))) {
  row <- tt_low_pass[i, ]
  case_str <- as.character(row$cases)
  case_ids <- as.integer(unlist(strsplit(gsub(" ", "", case_str), ",")))
  cases_info <- case_lookup %>% filter(case_id %in% case_ids)
  
  # Extract condition values safely
  config_vals <- as.numeric(row[cond_cols])
  config_parts <- ifelse(config_vals == 1, cond_cols, paste0("~", cond_cols))
  config_label <- paste(config_parts, collapse = "*")
  
  n_tourist <- sum(cases_info$Tourism == 1)
  n_total   <- nrow(cases_info)
  
  # Extract and convert consistency to numeric
  consistency <- as.numeric(row$incl)
  
  cat(paste0("Config: ", config_label, "\n"))
  cat(paste0("  Consist: ", round(consistency, 3),
             "  |  N=", n_total,
             "  |  Tourist: ", n_tourist, "/", n_total,
             " (", round(n_tourist / n_total * 100, 0), "%)\n"))
  
  for (j in seq_len(nrow(cases_info))) {
    marker <- ifelse(cases_info$Tourism[j] == 1, " [T]", "")
    cat(paste0("    #", cases_info$case_id[j], " ",
               cases_info$nom_barri[j],
               " (sat=", round(cases_info$satisfaction[j], 2), ")",
               marker, "\n"))
  }
  cat("\n")
}

```


## 8.3 Tourism concentration summary

```{r}
cat("=== TOURISM CONCENTRATION SUMMARY ===\n\n")
cat("Baseline: 11 tourist / 73 total = 15.1%\n\n")
# High satisfaction
all_high_ids <- c()
tour_high_ids <- c()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(tt_high_pass))) {
  ids <- as.integer(unlist(strsplit(gsub(" ", "", as.character(tt_high_pass$cases[i])), ",")))
  all_high_ids <- c(all_high_ids, ids)
  tour_high_ids <- c(tour_high_ids, ids[ids %in% case_lookup$case_id[case_lookup$Tourism == 1]])
}
all_high_ids <- unique(all_high_ids)
tour_high_ids <- unique(tour_high_ids)

cat("HIGH SATISFACTION paths:\n")
cat(paste("  Total cases:", length(all_high_ids), "\n"))
cat(paste("  Tourist:", length(tour_high_ids),
          "(", round(length(tour_high_ids)/length(all_high_ids)*100, 1), "%)\n"))
cat(paste("  Tourist NOT in any path:",
          paste(case_lookup$nom_barri[case_lookup$Tourism == 1 &
            !(case_lookup$case_id %in% all_high_ids)], collapse = ", "), "\n"))

```

## 8.4 Export tourism mapping

The case-level mapping is saved for reference, including each case's membership in the outcome, so deviant cases (members of a sufficient configuration without the outcome) can be identified.

```{r save-tourism-mapping}
map_configs <- function(tt_pass, outcome_label, outcome_col) {
  rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(tt_pass)), function(i) {
    row      <- tt_pass[i, ]
    case_ids <- as.integer(unlist(strsplit(gsub(" ", "", as.character(row$cases)), ",")))
    vals     <- as.numeric(row[cond_cols])
    label    <- paste(ifelse(vals == 1, cond_cols, paste0("~", cond_cols)), collapse = "*")

    case_lookup %>%
      filter(case_id %in% case_ids) %>%
      mutate(outcome            = outcome_label,
             tt_row             = rownames(tt_pass)[i],
             configuration      = label,
             consistency        = round(as.numeric(row$incl), 3),
             PRI                = round(as.numeric(row$PRI), 3),
             n_cases            = length(case_ids),
             outcome_membership = round(qca_data[[outcome_col]][match(case_id, as.integer(rownames(qca_data)))], 3),
             has_outcome        = ifelse(outcome_membership > 0.5, "Yes", "No (deviant)"))
  })
  bind_rows(rows)
}

tourism_mapping <- bind_rows(
  map_configs(tt_high_pass, "High satisfaction", "SATISF"),
  map_configs(tt_low_pass,  "Low satisfaction",  "SATISF_NEG")
) %>%
  mutate(tourist = ifelse(Tourism == 1, "Yes", "No")) %>%
  select(outcome, tt_row, configuration, consistency, PRI, n_cases,
         case_id, codi_barri, nom_barri, tourist, satisfaction,
         outcome_membership, has_outcome)

write.csv2(tourism_mapping,
           file = here("2_QCA", "Results", "Tourism_mapping", "tourism_mapping_cases.csv"),
           row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")

cat("Tourism mapping saved:", nrow(tourism_mapping), "rows\n")
```

## 8.5 Export truth tables for the appendix

```{r export-truth-tables}
if (!require("writexl")) install.packages("writexl")
library(writexl)

format_truth_table <- function(tt) {
  t <- tt$tt
  t <- t[t$n > 0, ]                                  # observed configurations only
  for (k in c("incl", "PRI", "OUT")) t[[k]] <- as.numeric(as.character(t[[k]]))
  t <- t[order(-t$incl, -t$n), ]

  case_names <- vapply(as.character(t$cases), function(cs) {
    ids <- as.integer(strsplit(gsub(" ", "", cs), ",")[[1]])
    cl  <- case_lookup[match(ids, case_lookup$case_id), ]
    paste0(cl$nom_barri, ifelse(cl$Tourism == 1, "*", ""), collapse = "; ")
  }, character(1))

  data.frame(Row = rownames(t),
             t[, cond_cols],
             n = t$n,
             Consistency = round(t$incl, 3),
             PRI = round(t$PRI, 3),
             OUT = t$OUT,
             Cases = unname(case_names),
             check.names = FALSE)
}

write_xlsx(
  list("High satisfaction" = format_truth_table(tt_high),
       "Low satisfaction"  = format_truth_table(tt_low)),
  path = here("2_QCA", "Results", "Sufficiency", "truth_tables_appendix.xlsx")
)

cat("Truth tables exported to Results/Sufficiency/truth_tables_appendix.xlsx\n")
```

# 9. Visualisations

## 9.1 XY plots for sufficiency assessment

XY plots display the relationship between each condition (X axis) and the outcome (Y axis). In a sufficiency relationship, cases should cluster below the diagonal; in a necessity relationship, above it. Points are colour-coded by tourism status.

```{r xy-plots-high, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
# Define the colour palette consistent with the PCA notebook
palette_tour <- c("0" = "#D3D1C7", "1" = "#8C4D59")

cond_full_names <- c(
  ECON = "Economic", HLTH = "Healthcare", HOUS = "Housing",
  INFR = "Infrastructure", MOBI = "Mobility", SOCI = "Social",
  URBN = "Urban environment"
)

for (cond in cond_cols) {
  p <- ggplot(qca_data, aes_string(x = cond, y = "SATISF")) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0,
                linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = factor(Tourism)),
               size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text_repel(aes(label = nom_barri, colour = factor(Tourism)),
                    size = 2, max.overlaps = 15, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = palette_tour,
                        labels = c("0" = "Non-tourist", "1" = "Tourist"),
                        name = "Neighbourhood type") +
    labs(x = paste(cond_full_names[cond], "(fuzzy membership)"),
         y = "High satisfaction (fuzzy membership)",
         title = paste("Sufficiency:", cond_full_names[cond],
                       "\u2192 High satisfaction")) +
    coord_fixed(ratio = 1, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    theme_minimal(base_family = "Arial", base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(colour = "#2C4019", face = "bold", size = 11),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )

  print(p)

  ggsave(filename = here("2_QCA", "Results", "Plots",
                          paste0("xy_high_", cond, ".png")),
         plot = p, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 300)
}
```

# 10. Robustness checks

Robustness checks assess the sensitivity of the results to alternative calibration thresholds and consistency cut-offs. This section tests two variations: (1) an alternative consistency threshold and (2) alternative calibration percentiles.

## 10.1 Sensitivity to consistency threshold

The main analysis uses a consistency cut-off of 0.80. Here, the analysis is repeated with a threshold of 0.75 and 0.85 to test whether the solution paths change.

```{r robustness-consistency}
run_intermediate <- function(data, outcome, dir_exp,
                             incl_cut = incl_cut_main, pri_cut = pri_cut_main) {
  tt <- truthTable(data = data, outcome = outcome, conditions = cond_cols,
                   incl.cut = incl_cut, pri.cut = pri_cut, n.cut = 1,
                   complete = TRUE, show.cases = TRUE, sort.by = c("incl", "n"))
  tryCatch(
    minimize(tt, include = "?", details = TRUE, show.cases = TRUE,
             dir.exp = dir_exp, method = "eQMC", row.dom = FALSE, first.min = FALSE),
    error = function(e) { cat("  FAILED:", e$message, "\n"); NULL }
  )
}

robustness_specs <- list(
  list(label = "HIGH satisfaction", outcome = "SATISF",     dir_exp = dir_exp_high),
  list(label = "LOW satisfaction",  outcome = "SATISF_NEG", dir_exp = dir_exp_low)
)

for (spec in robustness_specs) {
  for (threshold in c(0.75, 0.85)) {
    cat("\n========================================\n")
    cat(" ", spec$label, "- consistency threshold:", threshold, "\n")
    cat("========================================\n")
    sol_rob <- run_intermediate(qca_data, spec$outcome, spec$dir_exp, incl_cut = threshold)
    if (!is.null(sol_rob)) print(sol_rob)
  }
}

```

## 10.2 Sensitivity to calibration anchors

The main calibration uses 25th/50th/75th percentiles. Here, the conditions are recalibrated using 20th/50th/80th percentiles and the analysis is repeated.

```{r robustness-calibration}
qca_data_alt <- qca_data

for (v in conditions) {
  qca_data_alt[[cond_labels[v]]] <- calibrate(
    qca_data[[v]], type = "fuzzy",
    thresholds = quantile(qca_data[[v]], c(0.20, 0.50, 0.80)))
}
qca_data_alt$SATISF <- calibrate(
  qca_data$satisfaction, type = "fuzzy",
  thresholds = quantile(qca_data$satisfaction, c(0.20, 0.50, 0.80)))

# 0.5 correction BEFORE computing the negated outcome
for (col in c("SATISF", cond_labels)) {
  qca_data_alt[[col]][qca_data_alt[[col]] == 0.5] <- 0.501
}
qca_data_alt$SATISF_NEG <- 1 - qca_data_alt$SATISF

for (spec in robustness_specs) {
  cat("\n=== ALTERNATIVE CALIBRATION (20/50/80) -", spec$label, "===\n")
  sol_alt <- run_intermediate(qca_data_alt, spec$outcome, spec$dir_exp)
  if (!is.null(sol_alt)) print(sol_alt)
}
```
